newsitem.title: UK: London gold teeters at support, silver tests lower.
newsitem.headline: London gold teeters at support, silver tests lower.

text.p: Gold was grasping onto $382 support in the afternoon but many players were becoming convinced it was gearing up for more falls, dealers said.
Gloom was also spreading to the other metals as silver dipped below its important floor of $5.05.
"Market participants have become increasingly bearish," said one dealer.
Gold fixed at $382.10 per ounce down 10 cents from the morning and compared to $383.50 on Wednesday afternoon.
Spot prices held in a tight range, probing down to $381.75, basis bids, and moving as high as $382.65.
Several dealers and analysts were expecting a short-covering bounce in the near-term since the market was seen as very short and oversold with an 14-day RSI below the benchmark 30 level.
Some thought this would happen when the market heard the result of a Friday meeting of the International Monetary Fund on whether it will sell a small portion of its gold reserves.
But any bounce was not expected to last long.
"Each time it rallies the highs are lower and people are quite happy to sell into the bounce," a dealer said.
If the key $380 floor from early July evaporated, the first support may be seen at $378, the lows from September 1995.
But a break below $380, the weakest price so far in 1996, could see some rapid moves as option-related selling kicks in, analysts said.
Some key lows the spot market has touched over the past few years include $373 in March 1995, around $371 in Janaury 1995 and $368 in April 1994.
Silver caught the chill and just before the afternoon fix slipped under its key level of $5.05, hitting a low bid of $5.02. It then managed a bounce back up above support.
Silver, which saw a high big of $5.09 so far, was seen largely tracking gold prices, dealers said.
Palladium -- which on Wednesday fixed at the worst levels since December 1993 -- notched up some fresh lows in the spot market.
Bids were quoted as low as $120.55, compared to a nadir of $121.25 on Wednesday, with a high bid seen at $122.00.
The steady downtrend was seen pushing lower, with some dealers targeting $110 as the goal.
Platinum was largely holding at softer levels hit in the morning, when it fixed at $390, the lowest level in two months. The range of bids has been $399.50 to $389.00.
